# K-210 Plant Air Compressor: Start, Stop, and Protection

Section scope: start, stop, and protection of K-210. Load control (IGV and FV-211 in the running state) is covered here only where it touches start, stop, or protection.

Assumptions are marked "TBD" and listed in section 9. I invented no values. Every number is in the lists in section 1.

## 1. Single source lists

### 1.1 Setpoint list (SP-K210)

| SP-01 | Lube header pressure, normal | PT-213 | 2.5 bar | Process |
| SP-02 | Lube header pressure, low alarm | PT-213 | 1.8 bar | Process |
| SP-03 | Lube header pressure, low-low trip | PT-213 | 1.3 bar | Process |
| SP-04 | Oil temperature, start permissive (minimum) | TT-214 | 25 °C | Process |
| SP-05 | Vibration, alarm (each stage) | VT-215/216/217 | 40 µm | Process |
| SP-06 | Vibration, trip (each stage) | VT-215/216/217 | 60 µm | Process |
| SP-07 | Discharge header pressure setpoint | Discharge PIC (tag TBD) | 7.0 barg | Process |
| SP-08 | Maximum starts per rolling hour | Motor | 3 | Motor vendor |

| SP-10 | PT-213 start permissive and P-212 stop pressure | PT-213 | TBD (OI-03) | Compressor vendor |

## 2. States and transitions

Automation level: the operator starts, loads, and stops. The sequences run automatically after the command (operator-prompted start).

| State | Meaning | Entry permissive | Allowed exits |
|---|---|---|---|
| STOPPED-NOT READY | One or more start permissives are false | Motor stopped, no trip active | STOPPED-READY |
| STOPPED-READY | All start permissives are true | See 3 | STARTING, STOPPED-NOT READY |
| STARTING | Start sequence runs | START command from operator | RUNNING-UNLOADED, TRIPPED |
| RUNNING-UNLOADED | Motor at full speed, IGV at minimum, FV-211 open | Start sequence complete | RUNNING-LOADED, STOPPING, TRIPPED |
| RUNNING-LOADED | Discharge pressure control active | LOAD command from operator | RUNNING-UNLOADED, STOPPING, TRIPPED |
| STOPPING | Unload, stop, and post-lube run | STOP command from operator | STOPPED-NOT READY, TRIPPED |
| TRIPPED | Protective action done, restart locked out | Any trip in section 6 | STOPPED-NOT READY (after RESET) |

| Transition | Initiator | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| STOPPED-READY to STARTING | Operator | START pushed and all permissives true |
| STARTING to RUNNING-UNLOADED | Auto | Step 8 of the start sequence complete |
| RUNNING-UNLOADED to RUNNING-LOADED | Operator | LOAD pushed; no active load inhibit |
| RUNNING-LOADED to RUNNING-UNLOADED | Operator | UNLOAD pushed |
| RUNNING-x to STOPPING | Operator | STOP pushed |
| STOPPING to STOPPED-NOT READY | Auto | Post-lube run complete |
| Any run state to TRIPPED | Auto | Trip cause in section 6 |
| TRIPPED to STOPPED-NOT READY | Operator | RESET pushed; all trip causes cleared; motor stopped |

## 3. Start permissives

Permissive logic is in the K-210 cause-and-effect chart (C&E-K210). This table lists the permissives and does not restate the logic.

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-K210-001 | The DCS shall show STOPPED-READY only when all permissives in C&E-K210 section "Start" are true. | FAT: force each permissive false; check START is rejected. |
| FR-K210-002 | TT-214 shall be above SP-04 as a start permissive. | FAT: simulate TT-214 across SP-04. |
| FR-K210-003 | The DCS shall switch the tank heater on when TT-214 is below SP-04 and K-210 is stopped. It shall switch the heater off above SP-04 plus SP-12. | FAT: simulate TT-214; check heater command. |
| FR-K210-004 | The DCS shall reject START if the starts in the last hour equal SP-08. | FAT: simulate start history. |
| FR-K210-005 | The DCS shall reject START if the time since the last hot start is below SP-09. | FAT: simulate start history. |
| FR-K210-006 | The DCS shall keep the start history valid after a DCS restart. | FAT: restart controller; check history. |
| FR-K210-007 | The DCS shall show the first false permissive on the K-210 faceplate. | FAT: visual check. |

## 4. Start sequence (SqBC)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Check all permissives (FR-K210-001). | All true | Immediate | Reject START. Show first false permissive. |
| 2 | Command FV-211 open. Command ZC-210 to minimum. | FV-211 open and ZT-210 at minimum | TM-01 | Abort start. Raise alarm. |
| 3 | Start P-212. | PT-213 above SP-10 | TM-02 | Stop P-212. Abort start. Raise alarm. |
| 4 | Keep P-212 running (pre-lube). | PT-213 stays above SP-10 for TM-03 | TM-03 | Abort start. Raise alarm. |
| 5 | Close the motor breaker. Command the soft starter to start. | Soft starter reports ramp active | TM-04 | Open breaker. Go to TRIPPED. |
| 6 | Wait for the soft starter to reach full voltage and close its bypass. | Bypass closed, motor current normal | TM-04 | Open breaker. Go to TRIPPED. |
| 7 | Check lube supply from the shaft-driven pump. Stop P-212 and set it to standby. | PT-213 above SP-10 with P-212 stopped | TM-05 | Keep P-212 running. Raise alarm. Continue. |
| 8 | Release the unloaded run. Enable the vibration trip (see FR-K210-011). | State is RUNNING-UNLOADED | Immediate | Not applicable. |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-K210-008 | The start sequence shall run steps 1 to 8 in order. | FAT: run sequence. |
| FR-K210-009 | The DCS shall not allow a motor start command before step 4 is complete. | FAT: fail each earlier step. |
| FR-K210-010 | The DCS shall count each START command that reaches step 5 as a start. | FAT: abort at step 5; check counter. |

## 5. Load, unload, and stop

### 5.1 Load and unload

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | Operator pushes LOAD. | Load inhibits clear | Immediate | Reject LOAD. Show reason. |
| L2 | Put the discharge pressure controller in AUTO at SP-07. | Controller in AUTO | TM-06 | Stay in RUNNING-UNLOADED. Raise alarm. |
| L3 | Let the controller open ZC-210. Let FV-211 close under the vendor surge control. | FV-211 closed | TM-06 | Hold present load. Raise alarm. |

FV-211 and ZC-210 can be commanded by both the vendor controller and the DCS. The surge demand always has priority (FR-K210-018). The ownership split is open (OI-01).

### 5.2 Normal stop

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Operator pushes STOP. Put the pressure controller in MANUAL. Command ZC-210 to minimum. Command FV-211 open. | ZT-210 at minimum and FV-211 open | TM-07 | Continue to step 2. Raise alarm. |
| 2 | Start P-212. | PT-213 above SP-10 | TM-02 | Raise alarm. Continue. |
| 3 | Command the soft starter to stop. Open the motor breaker. | Motor stopped | TM-08 | Trip the upstream breaker (C&E-K210). Raise alarm. |
| 4 | Keep P-212 running after zero speed. | TM-09 elapsed | TM-09 | Not applicable. |
| 5 | Stop P-212. Set it to standby. | P-212 stopped | Immediate | Not applicable. |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-K210-011 | The DCS shall inhibit the vibration trip for TM-10 after the motor start command. The vibration alarm stays active. | FAT: simulate vibration above SP-06 during run-up. |
| FR-K210-012 | A failed unload (STOP step 1) shall not prevent the motor stop. | FAT: hold ZT-210 off minimum during STOP. |
| FR-K210-013 | The DCS shall keep P-212 running from the STOP command until TM-09 elapses after zero speed. | FAT: run stop; check P-212 status. |

## 6. Protection

The vendor controller holds surge protection. The DCS and motor protection relay hold the other items. If the SRS assigns any of these to a SIF, the SRS governs and this section only references it (OI-02).

### 6.1 Protection requirements

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-K210-014 | Trip K-210 when PT-213 is below SP-03. | FAT: simulate PT-213 below SP-03. |
| FR-K210-015 | Trip K-210 when any of VT-215, VT-216, VT-217 is above SP-06. | FAT: test each probe. |
| FR-K210-016 | Alarm when PT-213 is below SP-02. Start P-212 when PT-213 is below SP-11. | FAT: simulate PT-213. |
| FR-K210-017 | Alarm when any vibration probe is above SP-05. | FAT: test each probe. |
| FR-K210-018 | The surge line in the vendor controller shall open FV-211. The DCS shall not close FV-211 while the vendor surge demand is active. | FAT: simulate surge demand during DCS close command. |
| FR-K210-019 | After a trip, lock out start until the operator pushes RESET and all permissives are true. | FAT: trip; try START. |

### 6.2 Trip actions

On any trip, the DCS shall do the following at the same time:

1. Open the motor breaker (and stop the soft starter).
2. Command FV-211 open.
3. Command ZC-210 to minimum.
4. Start P-212.
5. Latch the first-out cause.

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-K210-020 | The DCS shall do all five trip actions for each trip cause in C&E-K210. | FAT: force each trip cause. |
| FR-K210-021 | P-212 shall start on a PT-213 low-low trip, even though the cause is lube pressure. | FAT: simulate PT-213 below SP-03; check P-212. |

## 7. Abnormal handling

| Condition | Required response | ID |
|---|---|---|
| PT-213 bad quality, stopped | Reject START. Raise alarm. | FR-K210-022 |
| PT-213 bad quality, running | Raise alarm. Start P-212. Do not trip on bad quality alone. | FR-K210-023 |
| TT-214 bad quality | Reject START. Switch the heater off. Raise alarm. | FR-K210-024 |
| One vibration probe bad quality | Raise alarm. Keep the other probes active. Reject START. | FR-K210-025 |
| ZT-210 bad quality | Reject START. Raise alarm. If running, hold load and alarm. | FR-K210-026 |
| Comms loss, DCS to vendor controller | Raise alarm. Reject START. Keep the run. The vendor controller keeps surge protection. | FR-K210-027 |
| Power loss, 6.6 kV | The motor stops. Go to TRIPPED. Do not restart automatically. | FR-K210-028 |
| Power loss, DCS or controller | Keep the start history (FR-K210-006). Go to TRIPPED on recovery if the motor is stopped. | FR-K210-029 |
| Power loss, AC auxiliary supply | P-212 cannot run during the coast-down. See OI-05. | FR-K210-030 |
| Fail positions | FV-211 fails to the position in OI-06. ZC-210 fails to the position in OI-06. | FR-K210-031 |

Test method for all rows in section 7: FAT or SAT simulation of the condition, and check of the listed response.

## 8. Operator interface

- Faceplate commands: START, STOP, LOAD, UNLOAD, RESET.
- Displayed: state, first false permissive, first-out trip cause, start count in the last hour, time to next allowed start, PT-213, TT-214, VT-215/216/217, ZT-210, FV-211 position, P-212 status.
- Prompts: "Start rejected", "Start aborted", "Trip". Each prompt shall name the cause. Operations signs off the prompt text (OI-07).
- Alarms: referenced from the rationalized alarm database (ISA-18.2). This section does not restate them.

## 10. Check against the review list

- **SSoT:** all values are in sections 1.1 and 1.2. No values appear in prose.
- **IDs and tests:** FR-K210-001 to FR-K210-031 each have a test method.
- **Sequences:** each step has a timeout and a failure response.
- **Abnormal cases:** bad PV, comms loss, power loss, and fail positions are in section 7, with gaps in OI-05 and OI-06.
- **Not done in this draft:** the full STE dictionary check and the ISA-106 level-of-automation review by operations. Both are still needed before issue.
